patch.objective: Creating and managing short-lived service account credentials

sources.cite: Google Cloud, Associate Cloud Engineer exam guide (PDF linked from the certification page): setting up a cloud solution environment (~20%), planning and implementing a cloud solution (~30%), ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution (~30%), configuring access and security (~20%)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-18. Four sections with the weights above match the course seed's units; subsections 3.3 'Managing networking resources' and 4.2 'Managing service accounts'; the guide names CMEK (3.2), Query Insights (3.4) and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (2.1, 3.1). The HTML page at cloud.google.com/certification/guides/cloud-engineer/ still shows an older five-section outline (Cloud Functions, Cloud Run for Anthos); the PDF is the current guide.

sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, IAM: Delete and undelete service accounts
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: deleting a service account immediately cuts off applications that use it; a new account with the same name is a separate identity that does not inherit the old one's roles; undelete works for 30 days; 'If you're unsure whether anything still uses an account, Google recommends disabling it instead of deleting it.' The 'Disable and enable service account keys' page (read 2026-11-18): gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable KEY_ID --iam-account=...; 'Disabling a service account key prevents you from using the key to authenticate with Google APIs', and it can be re-enabled. The audit log fields are authored renderings.
